key_insight: A robust reinforcement learning framework can learn adaptive cancer treatment policies that stay effective across different patients and remain reliable despite biomarker error and shifts in disease dynamics.
clinical_relevance: For precision oncology, this approach could help design more dependable adaptive therapy strategies, especially when patient measurements are imperfect or disease behavior changes over time.
method: Models each patient as a hidden context to capture between-patient variability.
Uses robust contextual Markov decision processes to jointly address generalization and uncertainty.
Tests the learned policy in a metastatic prostate cancer simulator calibrated to clinical data.
evidence_signal: In simulator evaluations calibrated to clinical data, the proposed policy outperformed the existing adaptive therapy method and Pareto-dominated it across a diverse range of scenarios.
watch_item: Results come from simulation, so real-world clinical impact still depends on prospective validation and careful handling of measurement and model mismatch.
paper_title: Robust Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Treatment Regimes under Model and Measurement Uncertainty
